audit_findings.title: The bridge may deduct a WAVE accounting balance that is not an enforceable economic claim
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $105.349 million, or $2.10 per share; removing the full balance would raise base value from $15.65 to approximately $17.75 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The balance is included in stakes_net and deducted from operating value in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: If it becomes probable that any excess distribution may not be returned, upon joint venture liquidation or otherwise, the liability balance will be immediately recognized as income.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the WAVE balance is an enforceable claim remains unresolved. However, even removing the entire filed $105.349 million balance leaves estimated base value near $17.75 and bull value near $19.74, both far below the $62.49 market price; the buy-below level would rise only from $10.96 to approximately $12.43. It therefore cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the WAVE venture agreement, guarantees, capital accounts and liquidation provisions; if no repayment obligation exists, rerun the bridge without the unsupported portion.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor contains a documented temporary channel load-in
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary A2L-related shipments and margins may inflate the $61.0 million owner-earnings anchor, which is projected through every scenario and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: As contractors, distributors, and dealers positioned inventory to adjust to the regulatory transition, order volumes were temporarily elevated above underlying demand.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that fiscal 2026 orders were temporarily above underlying demand and began normalizing in the fourth quarter. It does not quantify the associated revenue, margin, working-capital benefit or fourth-quarter unwind, so the record cannot establish the required anchor adjustment or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain quarterly A2L-related shipments, gross margin and working-capital data, normalize fiscal 2026 to sell-through demand, and rerun all scenarios using the normalized owner-earnings anchor.

audit_findings.title: Unpaid LSI purchase consideration is not identifiable in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $3.0 million, or approximately $0.06 per share; full deduction would reduce base value from $15.65 to approximately $15.59 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid acquisition consideration is a direct claim on equity and belongs in the valuation bridge unless already included in another liability adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: The purchase price was $ 206,559 , net of cash acquired, and includes an estimated tax equalization payment of approximately $ 3,000 that was not settled at closing.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that approximately $3.0 million was unsettled at closing, while the May 31 purchase-price allocation remained open. Even if the entire amount remained unpaid and was wholly omitted from the bridge, the resulting reduction is about $0.06 per share and does not affect the valuation conclusion relative to the $62.49 market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the tax equalization payment to May 31 accrued liabilities and subsequent cash settlement; deduct it only if still payable and not already captured elsewhere.

audit_findings.title: The performance-award amount does not establish a true dilution ceiling
audit_findings.mechanism: Above-target settlement would increase the fully diluted share denominator beyond the included 0.100009 million performance shares and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: Includes common shares related to previously granted awards that paid out at percentages above target levels.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that awards can pay above target, but supplies no maximum payout percentages. The included target balance equals only about 0.20% of the 50.077535 million-share denominator, yet the absent contractual ceiling prevents establishing the maximum dilution or conclusively determining materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the governing award agreements or proxy disclosures, calculate maximum issuable shares for each outstanding tranche, and rerun per-share values with the no-offset ceiling denominator.

audit_findings.title: Mixing a July cover count with May award balances may double-count vested awards
audit_findings.magnitude: at most 1.143119 million shares within the supplied denominator; removing every share added above the 48.934416 million cover count would raise base value from $15.65 to approximately $16.02 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Awards issued between May 31 and July 23 may appear both in the July outstanding-share count and in the May award inventory added to the diluted denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of common shares (the only common equity of the registrant) outstanding, as of July 23, 2026 , was 48,934,416 .
audit_findings.explanation: The date mismatch creates a genuine reconciliation issue, but the entire difference between the supplied fully diluted denominator and July cover count is only 1.143119 million shares. Even the extreme assumption that every added share is duplicated changes base value by about $0.37 per share and leaves it far below the $62.49 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile May 31 through July 23 issuances, vestings, forfeitures and tax withholdings, then remove any demonstrated duplicates from the denominator.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.1 million of FY2024 D&A; $0 effect on the current $61.0 million latest-actual anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible residual D&A would increase FY2024 owner earnings, but the valuation uses fiscal 2026 latest actual rather than the interrupted historical trend as its anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2024 $32.1m (39.8% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment may understate fiscal 2024 owner earnings, but fiscal 2024 is not the operative anchor and the model expressly rejects a trend because of missing years and repeated sign changes. Reclassifying the full identified residual therefore does not directly change the current anchor or valuation conclusion under the stated method.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $32.1 million residual from filed asset and expense disclosures; if any portion qualifies for addition, recompute FY2024 owner earnings and confirm that the anchor-selection ruling remains latest actual.
